youtube.title: WEDNESDAY WEBINARS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Kathryn Ennis-Carter run through a big week of local government news, from Stuart Smith's Members Bill and the Local Government Systems Improvement Bill to Simon Watts' proposed 4% rates cap and stalled amalgamation proposals. They work through listener questions covering rates affordability, water charges, residential parking fees, council staffing and contract transparency, plus the Mount Maunganui disaster report, urging ratepayers to use LGOIMA requests to hold councils accountable. Catch Simon O'Connor's talking with Stuart Smith about his Local Government Management of Local Authorities Amendment Bill. For more on the Mount Maunganui disaster report, check out RCR's A Political Agenda Want the local government stories others miss? Get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: MEDIA MATTERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Marty Gibson discuss the perceived media and political “free pass” given to Chris Hipkins, including his handling of COVID-19 and vaccine rollout issues. They also examine proposed social media restrictions for under-16s, arguing these could expand government control and digital ID systems. The hosts compare Hipkins and Christopher Luxon as technocratic leaders and question whether major parties are increasingly selecting candidates who prioritise party compliance over independent representation. For more on Myocarditis Risk in Teens Read more about the evidence and events surrounding the Covid-19 response in The People's Position and The People's Report and see RCR's updated myocarditis timeline. RCR Bites Lead Story: Labour backs under-16 social media ban, but Government says no time for vote Say No to Digital ID campaign Check out this three-part series with Maree Buscke and independent journalist Bonnie Flaws exploring the rollout of Digital ID in New Zealand: Part 1 , Part 2 and Part 3 For all the news you need this election season, get RCR Bites delivered FREE every weekday

youtube.title: NICK HUDSON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with Nick Hudson, chairman of Pandemics, Data & Analytics (PANDA), who argues Anthony Fauci is merely a “controlled asset” sustaining a false pandemic narrative. Hudson ranges widely across contested territory, dismissing 9/11 and October 7 as false flags, calling vaccines and cancer screening a scam, and framing conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East as covers for food-chain disruption, while reflecting on feeling alienated from those he calls “normies.” Discover more from Nick on X and PANDA There’s always more to the story. Get RCR Bites , FREE every weekday

youtube.title: SAM UFFINDELL
youtube.summary: National MP Sam Uffindell spoke with Simon O’Connor about the fatal Mount Maunganui landslide that killed six people, with a recent report finding it was preventable despite warnings spanning 25 years. Uffindell criticised Tauranga City Council’s lack of accountability, its handling of affected businesses, and a controversial land deal where the council sold prime land near the Harbour Bridge for $13.9 million, despite estimates valuing it at $20–33 million. The council then committed $29 million to fund a wharf for the developer and provided $9.5 million in vendor finance. For more on Sam Uffindell and on Facebook For more on the Mount Maunganui landslide: A Political Agenda with Maree Buscke, Ro Edge & David Lynch Get the election news that matters — RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: BERNADETTE SOARES
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke talks with New Zealand First's Upper Harbour candidate about her move from Vision NZ and New Conservative to New Zealand First. They discuss the cost-of-living pressures she's hearing on the campaign trail, and her strong opposition to the proposed India free trade agreement. She also reflects on how immigration settings have changed since she arrived from India in 1989. Discover more from Bernadette Soares and on X For all the news you need this election season, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: MONEY TALKS
youtube.summary: Simon Angelo and Paul Brennan discuss the shift away from New Zealand property as the dominant path to wealth, arguing that shares and productive businesses may offer stronger long-term returns. They also examine falling graduate employment, the shortage of skilled trades, AI’s impact on jobs, New Zealand’s manufacturing base, and Angelo’s concerns about proposed tax policies and MMP voting ahead of the election. Discover more from Simon at Wealth Morning Look beyond the headlines. Get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: THE FOURTH ESTATE
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke is joined by former judge David Harvey and political commentator Ani O’Brien to examine the proposed social media restrictions, age verification, privacy and the growing power of government regulators. They also discuss media coverage of the teen myocarditis story, how media represents the leaders of the various political parties, MMP election strategies, and who is to blame for the death of disgraced academic Jason Arday – the media, or the establishment that created him. For more information David's substack – A Halfling's View Ani's substacks Thought Crimes and Women’s Rights & Wrongs , and find her on X Look beyond the headlines with RCR Bites , FREE every weekday

youtube.title: STUART SMITH
youtube.summary: Simon O'Connor talks to Stuart Smith, MP for Kaikoura and Chief Government Whip, about the gravel and flooding crisis plaguing local rivers since the Kaikōura earthquake, and the consenting delays blocking proactive fixes. They also discuss Smith's Local Government Management of Local Authorities Amendment Bill, giving councillors real oversight over chief executives, and how the public can make submissions before the select committee deadline. For more on Stuart Smith and on Facebook Have your say on the Local Government (Management of Local Authorities) Amendment Bill For all the news you need this election season, RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: RACHEL MATHEWS & MADELEINE HUNT
youtube.summary: A timely Council Watch discussion with Maree Buscke and Kathryn Ennis-Carter, and with author, educator & Council Watch activist Rachel Matthews, and Heritage Party General Secretary & civic accountability advocate Madeleine Hunt, exploring local government reforms in the UK and New Zealand. The panel examines growing centralisation, regional mayoral structures, council accountability, legal challenges, funding pressures and the influence of global initiatives on local decision-making. For more information National Residents for Civic Accountability (NRCA) Madeleine’s Substack Council Watch (Colchester & Countrywide!) youtube.title: ROSS COLLETT
youtube.summary: Rodney Hide speaks with Ross Collett, who was diagnosed with terminal pancreatic cancer and given just 2–3 months to live. Ross chose to pursue alternative treatments, including hyperbaric oxygen therapy, and has now completed more than 230 sessions. More than a year on, he remains active, optimistic and determined to make the most of his time. Disclaimer: This interview shares Ross Collett’s personal experience and views on cancer treatment. It is not medical advice or a recommendation for any particular treatment. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional before making decisions about your health or treatment. For more on Wellington Hyperbaric There’s always more to the story. Get RCR Bites , FREE every weekday

youtube.title: CAMERON LUXTON
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with ACT Party MP Cameron Luxton about the Mount Maunganui tragedy and calls for accountability, ACT’s push to strengthen the rule of law and protect property rights, local government reform and rates, and whether tactical voting could reshape the Coalition’s prospects at the upcoming election. Discover more from Cameron on Facebook and X For all the news you need this election season, get RCR Bites , delivered FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: DR GUY HATCHARD
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with health and food-safety advocate Dr Guy Hatchard about mounting pressure on New Zealand’s hospitals, rising excess deaths, falling birth and fertility rates, and increasing infant mortality. They question whether authorities are properly monitoring these trends and examine possible pandemic-era consequences, gene-based medicine, nutrition, lifestyle and political accountability. Dr Hatchard argues that New Zealand urgently needs to confront its deteriorating health indicators rather than ignore them. For more from Guy in the Hatchard Report: Red Flag: NZ mortality up in 2026 Look beyond the health headlines. youtube.title: WINSTON PETERS
youtube.summary: Winston Peters joins Paul Brennan for a wide-ranging discussion covering New Zealand First’s opposition to the proposed under-16 social media ban, concerns over age verification and civil liberties, coalition tensions, and plans to challenge Fonterra’s dairy monopoly. Discover more from Winston Peters on X and Facebook Look beyond the headlines this election season. Get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: PAUL’S MAILBAG
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan catches up on some of his latest mail, responding to listener feedback on roadside drug testing, AI data centres and surveillance, mandatory folic acid fortification in the UK, and ongoing demands for COVID accountability. He also covers concerns about the proposed 1080 poison drop, bird flu, the over 311,000 teenagers who received a second COVID shot after the government knew of the risk of myocarditis, and a listener’s experience with a submission being returned under the HSNO Amendments Bill process. youtube.title: MICHAEL ARBON
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon examines whether Australia’s compulsory superannuation system has delivered on its promise of reducing reliance on the age pension. He looks at rising contribution rates, changing tax rules, the enormous pool of money now controlled by super funds, and the economic opportunity cost for households. Arbon argues that directing super towards mortgages could dramatically reduce debt and asks whether Australians should have more freedom over their own money.
